a: Breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems that can be solved separately
tasks.fb: Not to be confused with abstraction, which removes detail rather than splitting it up.

tasks.q: How do you know when to stop decomposing?
a: When each part is small enough to be solved or programmed on its own
When the diagram fills the page
tasks.fb: There is no fixed number of levels.

tasks.q: Which are genuine advantages of decomposition? Select all that apply.
opts: Each part can be tested on its own
Several programmers can work at once
Parts can be reused in other programs
Smaller parts are easier to understand
It removes the need for testing
correct: Each part can be tested on its own
Several programmers can work at once
Parts can be reused in other programs
Smaller parts are easier to understand
tasks.fb: Speed is not one of them, and testing becomes easier rather than unnecessary.

tasks.q: A team of five is writing a shop system. How does decomposition help them?
a: Each person takes a separate part, such as payments or stock, and they can work at the same time
It halves the number of bugs
It removes the need to plan
tasks.fb: Splitting the work is only possible once the problem is split.

tasks.q: What does a structure diagram show?
a: How a problem breaks down into parts, from the whole system at the top to the detail below
The order the program runs in
tasks.fb: It shows structure, not sequence: that is what a flowchart is for.

tasks.q: Put these levels of a structure diagram for a music app in order, from top to bottom.
steps: Add a track, Remove a track, Rename a playlist
Check the track exists, Write it to the playlist file
tasks.fb: Each level breaks the one above into its parts.

tasks.q: In a quiz program, which level does each part belong to?
items: Compare the answer to the correct one
Print the question text on screen
tasks.fb: Main parts are jobs; detailed steps are things you could write in one or two lines.

tasks.q: Why is the bottom level of a structure diagram useful to a programmer?
a: Each box there is small enough to be written as a few lines or one subprogram
It shows which language to use
tasks.fb: That is the point of splitting until the parts are small.

tasks.q: Is each decision abstraction or decomposition?
items: Deciding the app does not need the car's colour
Splitting the app into find a space, pay, and extend a stay
Separating the payment code from the map code
Storing only the space number, not its exact position
Writing 'check space is free' as its own subprogram
tasks.fb: Remove detail, or split into parts: two different jobs.

tasks.q: Why does abstraction usually come first?
a: You need to know what the problem really is before you can split it into the right parts
Because the exam asks for it first
tasks.fb: Split the wrong problem and every part is wrong.

tasks.q: Which is the strongest exam answer?
a: The system splits into borrow, return, search and fines; each can be written and tested separately, and search can be reused elsewhere
The system is broken into smaller parts
tasks.fb: Named parts plus a stated benefit.

tasks.q: A question asks for a structure diagram. What loses marks most often?
a: Writing a list of steps in order instead of a tree of parts
tasks.fb: A structure diagram shows what the parts are, not the order they run in.

tasks.q: Which level of the structure diagram does each item belong to?
items: Add an item to the basket
Check the card number is 16 digits
Send the driver's position to the app
tasks.fb: Main parts are jobs the system does; detailed steps are things you could code directly.

info.title: Also called top-down
info.text: Structure diagrams are sometimes called top-down design, because you start with the whole and work down into detail.

info.title: Hidden problems
info.text: Decomposing usually uncovers parts nobody thought of, which is one of the best reasons to do it before writing code.

info.title: Divide and conquer
info.text: Some algorithms decompose as they run: merge sort splits a list in half over and over, which you meet later in this topic.

info.title: Real teams
info.text: A large app may have hundreds of modules. No one person knows them all, which is only possible because the problem was decomposed.

info.title: Reuse pays twice
info.text: A well-separated 'check a date is valid' subprogram gets used in five places and tested once.

info.title: Exam wording
info.text: Watch for 'state the advantages of decomposition': the marks are for named benefits, not a definition.
